- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is rising, model may underreact; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing upward momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.5) and recent price trend is upward; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong moves; apply a smoothing filter or reduce volatility in forecast tails.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent peak, model tends to overpredict; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underpredicts; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid missing bottom.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) — use sentiment-weighted average to stabilize forecast.
